title: Scalable Fabrication of Stretchable, Dual Channel, Microfluidic Organ Chips
protocol: Clean work area using packing tape and wipe down with cleanroom wipes and isopropyl alcohol.
Mix PDMS at a ratio of 10:1 (10 g cross linking agent, 100 g elastomer base) by hand or with a commercially available mixer.
Use a planetary centrifugal mixer to mix for 2 minutes at 2000 rpm.
Degas the mixed PDMS for 2 minutes at 2200 rpm.
Clean molds with an air gun before use.
Wipe down the glossy side of each polyurethane piece with ethanol and cleanroom wipes, ensuring all residual ethanol is dried from the surface.
Place the glossy side of the polyurethane over the open side of the MiP mold to create a seal, leaving only a well-like opening for pouring PDMS.
Check that every mold is covered securely by the polyurethane piece to prevent PDMS leakage during pouring.
Place the mold and polyurethane assemblies into the MiP jig with the textured side against the end of the MiP jig.
Tighten the MiP jig by turning the handle using a wrench until the jig spacing is 25 mm in width.
Create a boat of aluminum foil surrounding the MiP jig to prevent excess PDMS from leaking onto surfaces.
Pour PDMS into each mold until full.
Place the jig filled with PDMS into a vacuum desiccator and pull vacuum at -80 kPa for 1 hour.
Remove the MiP jig from the desiccator and place it in a 60 °C oven for at least 4 hours to cure the PDMS.
Disassemble the MiP jig using a wrench by turning the handle counter clockwise.
Remove molds from the jig once free from compression.
Discard polyurethane strips from each mold.
Carefully de-mold PDMS parts and lay them feature-side up.
Cut away each end of the top components at the end tab notch with a tile scraper.
Inspect PDMS parts for scratches, debris, bubbles, or deformation; discard unsatisfactory parts.
Store finished PDMS parts in square Petri dishes within pressure positive cabinets at room temperature.
Pour approximately 10.5 g of PDMS into molds until it reaches the top of the cavity.
Inspect the bottom channel mold for any cured PDMS on the bottom and scrape off if necessary to ensure an even surface.
Use an air gun very gently to move PDMS over uncovered small areas less than 2 cm².
Place molds into vacuum desiccator for 1 hour.
Move molds into a level 60 °C oven after 1 hour, for more than 4 hours.
Loosen PDMS from one edge of the mold using forceps.
Grip one corner and gently peel back PDMS from the mold surface.
Lay PDMS on work surface with channel features face up.
Cut parts along outside edges with tile cutters, placing blade in notched PDMS.
Lay parts feature side up on tape to remove debris.
Remove part from packing tape carefully.
Drag loose end of the part across a slide to laminate with glass.
Check parts for any failure modes including scratches, large debris, large bubbles, or deformed vacuum channels.
Discard unsatisfactory parts based on quality control inspection.
Cover features with tape.
Store parts in a positive pressure cabinet at room temperature.
Place each membrane wafer in designated slots of AMF trays.
Use 1 mL syringe to place 0.09 mL of PDMS onto the center of each membrane wafer post array.
Let PDMS sit for a minimum of 5 minutes to spread throughout the posts of the membrane wafer.
Plasma treat the polycarbonate strip at 20 W for 45 s, O₂ gas at 0.80 mbar in a plasma machine.
Remove the polycarbonate sheet from the plasma machine and cut into 45 mm x 45 mm squares.
Gently lay the plasma treated side of the polycarbonate squares onto the liquid PDMS centered on the membrane wafer.
Ensure that the polycarbonate and the PDMS are in contact, avoiding air pockets.
Place the pre-cut PDMS spacer on the center of the polycarbonate square.
Place the pre-cut textured polycarbonate sheet on the PDMS block to keep the assembly from bonding to the compression plate.
Insert tray so that Tray 3 is in the back, Tray 2 is in the middle, and Tray 1 is in the front.
Open the output pressure valve and very slowly open the input pressure valve.
Close the output pressure valve.
Flip the AMF switch to ON to begin the curing cycle.
Cure wafer under 4 kg (16 kPa) of compression.

Follow the temperature ramping cycle: start at 20°C for 20 minutes, then increase to 35°C for 10 minutes, then to 45°C for 10 minutes, then to 50°C for 60 minutes, and finally to 60°C for 120 minutes.
Hold at 20°C after the temperature cycle is complete.
Close the input pressure valve.
Open the output pressure valve to release pressure from the air cylinders.
Remove the trays and bring them to the laminar flow hood.
Carefully peel off the textured polycarbonate.
Carefully remove the PDMS spacer, ensuring it does not also peel off the polycarbonate carrier; if this occurs, start peeling from a different corner.
Inspect the PDMS membrane through the polycarbonate carrier for areas with through-holes and use a marker to trace the outline of the through-hole area and mark any holes or defects in the membranes.
Using wafer handling forceps, loosen wafers from the tray.
Remove each membrane from the wafer and place it in a Petri dish.
Clean the PDMS membranes as well as the insides of the Petri dish to remove debris using matte tape.
Thoroughly tape the feature side of each top component to remove debris.
Place top channel part ("top") feature side up in Petri dish with PDMS membrane.
Load the Petri dishes into the plasma machine.
Plasma treat membrane and top at 20 W for 45 s, O2 gas at 0.80 mbar.
Remove the dishes from the plasma machine once bonding cycles are finished.
Lay the activated parts feature side down on top of the membrane to ensure full lamination with no bubbles.
Place parts into a 60 °C oven for at least 2 h to anneal.
Using a scalpel, trace around the perimeter of the bonded top to separate top-membrane assembly from the polycarbonate carrier.
Peel the assembly from the polycarbonate.
Remove the PDMS membrane from the ports that access the bottom channel using sharp tipped forceps.
Under a stereoscope, remove any debris or dust with forceps under the stereoscope.
Place the feature side up assemblies with bottom components into the plasma machine.
Plasma treat assemblies with bottom components using the conditions in step 5.5.
Align the top assembly with microscope slide to the bottom half under an inverted microscope.
Place aligned assemblies in a 60 °C oven for at least 2 h.
Tug lightly on each corner of the chip to check for delaminating parts.
Look at the channel of the chip to check for a wrinkled or sagging membrane.
Inspect main channel and vacuum channels for debris under the microscope.
Check that the main channels are aligned to within 50-60 µm.
Ensure that the channels do not overlap with vacuum channels.
Check that the membrane between the main channels and inlet/outlet channels is intact without any holes.
Store chips in Petri dishes in a positive pressure cabinet at room temperature.
